chunks: We were seated in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when al-A'la ibn Kamil came and sat in front of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: Supplicate to Allah that He may provide me [sustenance] in ease. So he (peace be upon him) said: I will not supplicate for you. Seek, just as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has commanded you.

key_terms.ادْعُ اللَّهَ: Supplicate to Allah — the act of du'a, calling upon God for a need
key_terms.اطْلُبْ: Seek — active striving and effort in pursuing one's livelihood
key_terms.دَعَة: Ease, tranquility, comfort — a life free of hardship and toil
key_terms.يَرْزُقَنِي: Provide me sustenance — rizq (provision) granted by God

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Sadiq refuse to make du'a for someone seeking provision in ease?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a striking exchange between Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) and a man named al-A'la ibn Kamil who came asking the Imam to pray for his provision in ease and comfort. Rather than fulfilling this request, the Imam declined, redirecting the man to take personal initiative and seek his livelihood as God has commanded. The teaching reflects a core Islamic ethic: du'a (supplication) is not a substitute for effort; one must act according to divine guidance and not rely on intercessory prayer as an escape from personal responsibility.
